scope: Formatting-only candidate for accepted Beagle Fox-01 and Catherine-01 groups. No link re-adjudication, accepted mutation or export.
method: Used accepted primary notes/decisions and direct source HTML. Evidence quotes are feature-bearing body passages with source pins; multipart dates, household voices, excluded annotations and receipt/dispatch boundaries are held explicitly.

requirements.requirement: Keep Darwin’s receipt of Fox’s two widely separated letters as a source-date statement, not as a single-date prompt.

evidence.quote: I received your two letters dated at the wide of interval of August & January.

requirements.notes: The May 23 1833 body reports receipt; the August/January dates belong to the incoming letters.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the July 1835 reply’s explicit receipt of June and November 1834 letters in inverted order; do not collapse their intervals.

evidence.quote: I have lately received two of your letters

requirements.notes: This is a multipart receipt statement, not evidence that both letters arrived together.

requirements.requirement: Keep the May–June header interval and the separate Susan/Owen letters in the body; do not convert the interval into one composition day.

evidence.quote: I have now altogether received three letters; your & Carolines together

requirements.notes: The body names distinct family inputs and a May 3 receipt for Susan/Owen; preserve each source role.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the explicit May receipt sequence and the later July 20/29 boundary in the related Catherine correspondence; do not merge family letters or dates.

evidence.quote: September 12th Caroline: October 14th. Catherine: November 12th. Susan: December 15th. Caroline: & Jan 13th. Caroline:

requirements.notes: This is Darwin’s acknowledgement list of incoming family letters; the date sequence is not a single prompt.

requirements.requirement: Render the July 20 header and body’s received-series boundary separately from the later July 29 section; receipt of the whole series is not one exact event.

evidence.quote: I have received the whole series of letters up to yours of November, 1833.

requirements.notes: The source is composed at sea and completed in port; retain its multipart date/receipt structure.

requirements.requirement: Preserve Caroline’s incoming account and its “letter back”/hearsay distinction; do not treat family reports as direct observation by Darwin.

evidence.quote: I had however heard excellent accounts of you tho‘ not from you

requirements.notes: The body explicitly separates heard reports from a letter received; source voice is Caroline.’s.

requirements.requirement: Keep Susan’s January 1834 family letter distinct from Darwin’s later response and its received Journal statement; do not infer physical delivery date beyond the body.

evidence.quote: Your Journal is safely packed up, now that we have all read it.

requirements.notes: The family reading and packing statement is incoming evidence; no synthetic Darwin prompt is supplied.

requirements.requirement: Render the MathML quarter-hour literally as 1/4 and retain the hurried Sullivan parcel/dispatch context.

evidence.locator: xpath://div[@id='letter']//div[@class='body-content']/p[contains(., 'I have only 1/4 of an hour to ')]

requirements.notes: The fraction is in Darwin’s authorial body; parcel dispatch does not prove Catherine’s receipt.

requirements.requirement: Keep the May 29 family letter’s third-party Captain Harding report separate from Catherine’s own voice and later Darwin answer.

evidence.quote: We have seen Capt Harding, since Caroline wrote to you; he came to consult Papa

requirements.notes: This is Susan/Catherine family correspondence and reported third-party information, not Darwin-authored evidence.

requirements.requirement: Preserve joint speaker boundaries: Caroline’s received letter, Catherine’s own text, and Papa’s message must remain attributable by section.

evidence.quote: Papa charges me to give you a message from him
evidence.locator: xpath://div[@id='letter']//div[@class='body-content']/p[contains(., 'Papa charges me to give you a ')]

requirements.notes: The body identifies Catherine as writer and explicitly relays Robert Waring Darwin’s message; do not flatten the household voices.

recommendations: Keep source headers, body sections, family relays, third-party reports, footnotes and annotations separate.
Render 1/4 MathML literally and retain broad/interval dates; receipt and dispatch are distinct events.
Do not export inferred prompts or merge repeated source material unless a verified artifact establishes duplication.
